chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Muhraz, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man left his daughter and his sister (from his father and mother).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth, all of it, is for the daughter, and there is nothing for the sister (from the father and mother).'
So I said, 'We have need for this ruling, and the deceased was a man from those people (non-Muslims), and his sister was a believer, understanding.'
He (peace be upon him) said, 'So take the half for her. Take from them as they take from you regarding their ways and their judgments.'
Ibn Udhaynah said, 'So I mentioned that to Zurara, so he said, 'Surely what Ibn Muhraz has come with is enlightening.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a daughter and her sister when the deceased is a non-Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of *al-khudhū minhum kamā ya’khudhūn minkum* (take from them as they take from you), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) adapts the daughter’s exclusive share to accommodate the sister in a mixed-faith context. Zarara’s endorsement of this ruling as 'light' highlights its jurisprudential clarity, demonstrating how Shia scholars apply flexible inheritance rules when dealing with non-Muslims or mixed families.
